statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). CME equity index futures reopened for the new Globex session at 22:00 UTC and NQ is trading near 29,462, up 0.04%, inside a narrow 29,457.50 to 29,490.25 band. Monday's cash session closed at 29,127.16, down 241.28 points or 0.82%, after opening 1.63% below the 29,368.44 previous close at 28,890.93, bottoming at 28,867.67 and recovering to 29,285.50. Nasdaq-100 futures had earlier recovered most of a 2.3% opening gap, trading from 29,107.25 to 29,604.50 before settling at 29,489.75. Both the decline and the recovery retraced inside the range, so no persistent one-way structure was established. The decline was also rotational rather than index-wide: the PHLX semiconductor index fell 5.9% while Microsoft gained 1.97% and Alphabet 3.22%. Cross-asset amplifiers eased into the close, with VIX settling at 17.10 below its 18.17 session high and the 10-year yield closing at 4.961%, negative on the day after trading through 5% to 5.012%. Tail is 15 in the low band; Stress remains high at 65 on the unresolved Saudi pipeline outage, with WTI near 101.99 and Brent near 106.32, and on a scheduled Federal Reserve decision on 16 September.
recommendation: Tail at 15 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The observed Globex reopen is orderly and narrow, which is the opposite of the structure that denies mean reversion. The danger window is retained at 13:00 to 15:00 UTC on 15 September, covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour, where a second consecutive gap open after a chip-led decline on the opening day of the FOMC meeting is the identified conditional risk. The conditional path holds the low band through the Asian session and the European morning, with small uplifts at the Tokyo open, the Hong Kong open and the European opening auction. It enters the watch band from 12:00 UTC ahead of the Empire State survey, peaks at 24 across the danger window, eases through the midday lull, and steps up again around the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC and into the pre-policy close. Stress remains high at 65 on an unresolved Middle East supply disruption, a 10-year yield that traded through 5% for the first time since 2023, and a semiconductor index down 5.9%. Stress alone does not change the mapped state.
headline: Globex reopens quietly with NQ near 29,462 in a 33-point band after Monday's 2.3% opening gap was largely recovered; with the decline rotational rather than index-wide and VIX settling below its session high, Tail eases to 15 in the low band
body:
The current hour carries genuine observed evidence rather than an evidence gap. CME equity index futures reopened at 22:00 UTC after the daily maintenance halt, and NQ has held a band only about 33 points wide, from 29,457.50 to 29,490.25, trading near 29,462 and up 0.04%. An orderly, narrow reopen is the single most direct piece of evidence against a pathological price path, and it is the main reason Tail eases from the previous hour.

Monday itself resolved as a two-sided session. Nasdaq-100 futures opened roughly 2.3% below the previous settlement, traded down to 29,107.25, rallied almost 500 points to 29,604.50 and settled at 29,489.75, down 0.66%. The cash index opened at 28,890.93, bottomed at 28,867.67, recovered to 29,285.50 and closed at 29,127.16, down 0.82%. Both the decline and the recovery retraced inside the range. That is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that overwhelms a mean-reversion profile.

The catalyst was concentrated rather than systemic. Over the weekend the chief executives of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI argued for slowing the pace at which the most capable AI models are advanced. Semiconductor exposure absorbed almost all of the reaction: the PHLX semiconductor index fell 5.9%, Nvidia lost 3.4%, Micron more than 5%, and Broadcom and AMD more than 4% each. Software moved the other way, with Microsoft up 1.97% and Alphabet up 3.22%, and ServiceNow, Adobe and Workday rallying 4% to 7.4%. A rotation of that shape reduces index-level directional efficiency even when the headline sector move is large, and megacap breadth ended the session split four up and four down. Separately, Bank of America fell 5.1% after its chief executive warned on investment banking fees, which is a financials story rather than a Nasdaq-100 one.

Cross-asset amplifiers are present but not aligned. Oil is the strongest of them: Saudi Arabia shut its East-West crude pipeline after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory, removing the main route that bypasses a Strait of Hormuz whose flows are already severely reduced, with repair estimates reported at five to six weeks. WTI is near 101.99 and Brent near 106.32. That fed the rates channel, and the 10-year yield traded to 5.012%, its first move through 5% since 2023, with the 30-year reaching 5.38%. Both retreated, and the 10-year closed at 4.961%, negative on the day, as buyers emerged. VIX rose 7.95% to 17.10 but settled below its 18.17 session high. Amplifiers that fade into the close are consistent with orderly price discovery rather than a developing one-way regime.

The scheduled backdrop is the two-day Federal Reserve meeting on 15 and 16 September, with the decision and projections due at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday and the press conference at 18:30 UTC. Market pricing reported after Friday's August inflation data has moved to roughly 90% for a 25 basis-point move, and Goldman Sachs changed its call accordingly. That repricing is an important source of Stress and of forecast dispersion, but on the calibration evidence available it is not by itself a reason to raise Tail before any policy-driven price path has been observed. The decision falls beyond the current 24-hour forecast window.

Within the window, the identified conditional risk is concentrated at the US cash open on 15 September. Monday gapped 1.63% lower at the cash open, and a second consecutive gap open, on the opening day of the FOMC meeting and with an unresolved oil supply shock, is the structure most capable of producing continuation that denies retracement. That is why the danger window is held narrowly at 13:00 to 15:00 UTC rather than being widened across the session, and why the conditional peak is 24, at the top of the watch band, rather than crossing into a blocking state on anticipation alone. Shared supplementary cross-asset context was older than the freshness threshold for this run and was used only as corroboration; every level cited above comes from independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail started the window at 22, eased to a 19 to 20 plateau through the Asian session, rose to a 26 peak during the European morning chip-led decline, repeated 26 at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon to 16 by the maintenance halt as the opening gap was recovered. Stress fell from a 79 peak to 66 and Confidence held between 78 and 89. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all concentrated in the chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low band through the remainder of the Asian session and the European morning, with small uplifts at the Tokyo cash open, the Hong Kong and mainland open and the European opening auction. It enters the watch band from 12:00 UTC ahead of the NY Empire State survey, peaks at 24 across the 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour, returns to the low end of the watch band in the midday lull, then steps up again for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC and into the final cash hour before the Federal Reserve decision. It returns to the low band in the 21:00 UTC maintenance halt. The Federal Reserve decision on 16 September falls beyond this window.
